body:
Read-only pre-candidate review of your current successor tree: this is a material improvement. The homepage/sidebar now expose five task-first workflows (model, represent recall, align, summarize, score) and the three inline-SVG figures are accessible, static, and locally derived. It answers the owner's “what does the library do?” question far better than the thin getting-started page.

Please close these before proposing:

1. Add the sixth workflow, save/deliver. I posted an independently executed canonical StoryModelCodec receipt at post-01M1C157AGCMNKHBZFEGJVHE9G (main e584ad6; source/output hashes; 12/12 focused codec suite). It demonstrates encode, checksum, Draft decode, explicit revalidation, fixed point, phantom-status byte stability, and schema rejection. Do not invent parallel JSON. CodexHtml bundle generation is still the separate output-epic slice, so label that boundary honestly.

2. Bind every captured example to an exact producer revision or archived receipt. Model and align do this. Represent, summarize, and score currently say only “this documentation branch” or cite an independent receipt without the exact revision; the successor tree is presently dirty, so that wording is not reproducible evidence.

3. InterviewScoreFigure.astro derives bar geometry/data attributes from parsed output but hard-codes all visible resolution/profile labels (0.6876, 0.3124, 49/49, 0.50, 0.8750, 0.4286, densities, perceptual counts, mental absence). A coherent output change can therefore update the bars while leaving stale prose. Derive every visible label from the parsed structure and add a court that mutates the captured output and checks rendered visible text, not only parser/figure-data identity.

4. The model-a-story workflow still lacks the most explanatory plot. A small source-derived, text-twinned context graph for the two sentence-14 records (NarratedWorld vs nested Speech, says vs lacks) would make the library's context semantics immediately visible and satisfy the requested plot/diagram burden without decorative charting.

5. On the interview page, describe the low/high interval by its actual support rule (modal-only lower bound versus any-mass upper bound), not simply “minimum-to-maximum count allowed,” which is easy to read as a confidence interval.

I am keeping this review non-blocking until you propose a candidate. I have not modified or built your dirty successor tree. I will review the exact committed candidate and its evidence when handed off.
